jobs.title: Senior Director, ALM Research & Analytics
jobs.description:
Job Description

What is the opportunity?

Lead RBC Corporate Treasury's quantitative ALM methodology development, modelling, research and analytics, focusing on interest rate risk measurement and management. Lead development of behavioral and market risk models, supporting pricing and risk measurement for non-trading on-balance sheet products, mortgage and loan commitments, securitization, and term funding. Interest rate risk represents the bank’s largest structural book market risk, with effective measurement and management critical for shareholder value preservation. The team you’ll lead also supports RBC’s Pension Investment Group modeling and measurement, across a diverse set of asset classes, strategies, and ALM topics.

What will you do?

Lead research, methodology and model development relating to structural interest rate risk, consumer behaviour econometric modeling and forecasting (e.g., prepayment, redemption, pull through, product flows, term / mix preferences), economic capital models, balance sheet dynamics, and retail product and embedded option pricing models, in RBC’s domestic and international banking book balance sheets
Lead development of diffusion, historic simulation, factor models, and deposit rate models in support of pricing, valuation, and risk measurement including economic capital, economic value and net interest income risk
Lead and / or collaborate in development and implementation of tools and disciplines to monitor, analyze and identify ALM risks, as required
Collaborate in development of hedging programs for retail banking product initiatives and campaigns, including mortgage, funding and securitization initiatives
Liaise with regulatory bodies to explain ALM models and parameters, and their performance, as required
Support pension investment, ALM, and risk measurement processes via development of requisite models, tools and analytics
Lead CT's model validation process with GRM, including collaborating with GRM to ensure effective model risk controls and governance, and managing IRRM team's model inventory and behavioural assumption assessment and monitoring schedule
Collaborate with Finance and Treasury partners to ensure alignment of ALM risk measurement, FTP, and financial performance management systems, as required
Explore and develop new techniques and approaches, including use of AI in ALM and model development
Lead and develop a team of high performing ALM modelling experts, providing ongoing staff direction, goal setting, and coaching

What do you need to succeed?

Must-have:

Graduate degree in a quantitative field such as financial engineering, mathematics, engineering, or economics
10+ years related experience with a strong grasp of ALM practices
Understanding of banking book balance sheet dynamics, product characteristics, client behaviour, and balance sheet flows, with focus on retail & commercial banking products
Solid understanding of financial principles and risk concepts, including financial modelling and engineering, pricing models, econometrics, and fixed income mathematics
Strong team management and coordination skills, ensuring accountability while fostering a positive, collaborative, and high-performing environment
Strong communication and negotiation skills
Well-organized and detail oriented, with ability to tailor analysis to required precision (i.e. 80/20 solutions) or attend to details, as needed
Strong understanding of applicable regulatory guidelines and accounting principles, and related systems

Nice-to-have:

CFA and / or FRM designations, or equivalent
Strong data and database skills, including SQL
Prior exposure to ALM risk engine platforms and software (e.g. QRM or similar)

What's in it for you?

We thrive on the challenge to be our best, progressive thinking to keep growing, and working together to deliver trusted advice to help our clients thrive and communities prosper. We care about each other, reaching our potential, making a difference to our communities, and achieving success that is mutual.

A comprehensive Total Rewards Program including bonuses and flexible benefits
Leaders who support your development through coaching and managing opportunities
Ability to make a difference and lasting impact
Work in an agile, collaborative, progressive, and high-performing team
The opportunity to interface with senior level executives from many different parts of the organization

Job Skills

Cash Management, Financial Regulation, Financial Services Industry, Knowledge Organization, Office Operations, Operational Risks, Risk Management, Standard Operating Procedure (SOP), Strategic Thinking, Treasury Management

jobs.title: Director, Digital Servicing
jobs.description:
You are as unique as your background, experience and point of view. Here, you’ll be encouraged, empowered and challenged to be your best self. You'll work with dynamic colleagues - experts in their fields - who are eager to share their knowledge with you. Your leaders will inspire and help you reach your potential and soar to new heights. Every day, you'll have new and exciting opportunities to make life brighter for our Clients - who are at the heart of everything we do.

At Sun Life, we're driven by our Purpose: helping our Clients achieve lifetime financial security and live healthier lives. Our values shape how we work: caring, authentic, bold, inspiring, and impactful.

When you join Sun Life, you'll work with passionate colleagues and empowering leaders who support your growth and celebrate your contributions, so you can make a meaningful difference in our Clients' lives.

Discover how you can make a difference in the lives of individuals, families and communities around the world.

Job Description:

The Director, Digital Servicing
role focuses on building strategy and executing initiatives that drive digital client self-service and channel shift outcomes. You'll be guided by your understanding of the digital health, wealth & protection landscape, clients, competitors, and strong relationships with business stakeholders.

What You'll Do

Work closely with Digital Channels, Adoption & Engagement, Member Journey, and Operations teams to understand call drivers and strategically reduce contacts by shifting users to IVR and digital channels
Partner with CCC & Operations leaders to identify call deflection and chat containment initiatives that minimize inbound call volume and shift client interactions to digital channels
Set clear strategy aligned with senior leadership and lead identification, evaluation, and prioritization of digital initiatives to enhance self-service and achieve channel shift outcomes
Partner cross-functionally to establish digital servicing roadmaps, define success metrics, and deliver technology-enabled solutions that improve experience while optimizing efficiency
Create and align OKRs measured and reported to leadership; leverage surveys, competitive intelligence, and customer data to prioritize features –
Drive digital journey containment by improving completion rates and reducing abandonment; track performance and provide strategic reporting
Lead cost-benefit analyses and benefit realization initiatives, providing executive-level insights into ROI and strategic value
Build and maintain a high-performing team through strategic talent development and performance management

What You Need To Succeed

Proven ability to influence senior leadership and navigate large, matrixed organizations at a senior level
Strong acumen in Agile delivery models and data-driven decision-making
Excellent analytical and problem-solving capabilities with ability to translate data into actionable insights
Collaborative communicator comfortable making decisions with limited information and encouraging experimentation
University degree in business, analytics, or computer science
5-10 years progressive experience in digital strategy, customer experience, or operations management
3-5 years in director-level or senior manager role leading cross-functional teams
Demonstrated experience with digital transformation and call center/client service optimization
Proven track record managing call deflection, IVR optimization, or digital channel containment initiatives (preferred)
Experience developing and delivering cost-benefit analyses and benefit realization programs
Background in financial services, insurance, or regulated industries
Proficiency with analytics platforms and data-driven decision-making
As this position is posted in several locations, we specify that bilingualism (French, English, both oral and written) is required for Quebec only for the frequent interactions with English and French-speaking colleagues or internal partners across Canada or worldwide

What’s in it for you?

Being a member of the Sun Life family, a group of people united by our Purpose: to help Clients and Employees achieve lifetime financial security and live healthier lives
An environment of continuous learning, development, and improvement
Our unique Sabbatical Program gives you the opportunity to take up to 6 weeks off, every five years
We are proud to be on the 2026 Best Workplaces in Canada list by Great Place to Work
We are thrilled to be recognized by Excellence Canada with their top-level certification, the Canada Order of Excellence for Mental Health at Work®, for prioritizing employee well-being, fostering a positive work culture, and achieving excellence in mental health

The Base Pay range is for the primary location for which the job is posted. It may vary depending on the work location of the successful candidate or other factors. In addition to Base Pay, eligible Sun Life employees participate in various incentive plans, payment under which is discretionary and subject to individual and company performance. Certain sales focused roles have sales incentive plans based on individual or group sales results.

Diversity and inclusion have always been at the core of our values at Sun Life. A diverse workforce with wide perspectives and creative ideas benefits our Clients, the communities where we operate and all of us as colleagues. We welcome applications from qualified individuals from all backgrounds.

Persons with disabilities who need accommodation in the application process, or those needing job postings in an alternative format, may e-mail a request to thebrightside@sunlife.com.

We are proud to be a hybrid organization that offers our employees the choice and flexibility to work from both the office and virtually based on the needs of the business, our Clients and you.

We may use artificial intelligence to support candidate sourcing, screening, interview scheduling.

We thank all applicants for showing an interest in this position. Only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

130,000/130 000 - 180,000/180 000

jobs.title: Technical Director, AI-Native Cloud & DevOps
jobs.description:
Why Valtech? We’re the experience innovation company - a trusted partner to the world’s most recognized brands. To our people we offer growth opportunities, a values-driven culture, international careers and the chance to shape the future of experience.

The opportunity

At Valtech, you’ll find an environment designed for continuous learning, meaningful impact, and professional growth. Whether you're pioneering new digital solutions, challenging conventional thinking or building the next generation of customer experiences, your work will help transform industries.

We Are Proud Of

The work we do and the innovation we drive
Our values of share, care and dare
A workplace culture that fosters creativity, diversity and autonomy
Our borderless, global framework, which enables seamless collaboration

The role

We are seeking a visionary and hands-on Technical Director to join our Cloud & DevOps Practice in Canada. This senior leadership role combines deep technical expertise, strategic consulting, solution architecture, and delivery leadership to help clients modernize their platforms, accelerate software delivery, and unlock value through cloud-native technologies and AI-powered solutions.

The ideal candidate brings extensive experience across Microsoft Azure
, modern web application architectures including Next.js
, and emerging Agentic AI technologies
. You will guide enterprise transformation initiatives, shape technical strategy, mentor engineering teams, and partner with business stakeholders to deliver innovative solutions at scale.

Role Responsibilities

Technical Leadership
Define and drive technical vision, architecture strategies, and best practices for cloud and DevOps engagements.
Lead the design and delivery of large-scale cloud-native solutions on Microsoft Azure.
Establish engineering standards, governance frameworks, security controls, and operational excellence practices.
Act as a trusted advisor to client executives, technology leaders, and product organizations.

Agentic AI & Innovation

Lead the design and implementation of Agentic AI solutions leveraging modern AI orchestration frameworks, LLMs, copilots, autonomous workflows, and intelligent agents.
Help clients identify opportunities to automate complex business processes through AI-driven systems.
Evaluate emerging AI technologies and define adoption strategies aligned with business objectives.
Architect secure, scalable, and responsible AI solutions within enterprise environments.

Cloud & DevOps Excellence

Drive cloud adoption, modernization, migration, and platform engineering initiatives.
Establish CI/CD pipelines, Infrastructure as Code (IaC), observability, reliability engineering, and cloud governance practices.
Guide platform teams in implementing scalable DevOps operating models and automation strategies.
Ensure solutions meet security, compliance, performance, and reliability requirements.

Delivery & Client Engagement

Lead multidisciplinary engineering teams across multiple engagements.
Support pre-sales, solutioning, technical discovery workshops, and proposal development.
Provide executive-level communication and technical leadership throughout project delivery.
Manage technical risk, architecture decisions, and delivery quality.

Talent Development

Mentor architects, engineers, and technical managers.
Foster a culture of innovation, continuous improvement, and technical excellence.
Contribute to capability development within the Cloud & DevOps practice.

Must Have Qualifications

10+ years of experience in software engineering, cloud architecture, platform engineering, or DevOps.
5+ years in technical leadership, architecture leadership, or consulting leadership roles.
Deep expertise in Microsoft Azure services, architecture patterns, governance, security, and operations.
Strong experience designing and delivering enterprise applications using Next.js, React, and modern web architectures.
Proven experience implementing or architecting Agentic AI, AI-enabled automation, autonomous workflows, copilots, or advanced AI solution frameworks.
Experience with cloud-native architectures, microservices, APIs, containers, and distributed systems.
Strong client-facing consulting experience with executive stakeholder management.
Microsoft Azure (App Services, AKS, Functions, AI Services, Networking, Security, Identity, Data Services, and Platform Engineering capabilities).
DevOps platforms and practices including GitHub, Azure DevOps, CI/CD, Infrastructure as Code, and automation.
Containers and orchestration technologies such as Docker and Kubernetes.
Modern JavaScript/TypeScript ecosystems.
Observability, monitoring, reliability engineering, and cloud security best practices.
AI and machine learning solution integration within enterprise applications.

Nice To Have Qualifications

Azure Solutions Architect Expert, Azure DevOps Engineer Expert, or other relevant Microsoft certifications.
Experience with Azure OpenAI Service and enterprise AI platform implementations.
Experience with platform engineering and internal developer platforms.
Background in consulting, digital transformation, or systems integration environments.
Experience leading distributed and global delivery teams.

If you do not meet all the listed qualifications or have gaps in your experience, we still encourage you to apply. At Valtech, we recognize that talent comes in many forms, and we value diverse perspectives and a willingness to learn.

Commitment to reaching all kinds of people

We design experiences that work for all kinds of people - and that starts with our own teams. At Valtech, we’re intentional about building an inclusive culture where everyone feels supported to grow, thrive and achieve their goals. No matter your background, you belong here. Explore our Diversity & Inclusion site to see how we’re creating a more equitable Valtech for all.

The Benefits

This is a 4 months temporary
position based in Canada
. The offered salary range is CAD $90 - 98 per hour
, depending on experience and location.

Your application process

Once you apply, our Talent Acquisition team will review your application. If your skills and experience align with the role, we’ll reach out for next steps. Your CV should cover key information on relevant experiences and expertise. We do not require information such as age, gender, marital status, or a headshot in your application. We review all candidates based on skills, experience, and potential.

⚠️ Beware of recruitment fraud: Only engage with official Valtech email addresses.

We are committed to inclusion and accessibility. If you need reasonable accommodations during the interview process, please either indicate it in your application or let your Talent Partner know.

About Valtech

Valtech is the experience innovation company that exists to unlock a better way to experience the world. By blending crafts, categories, and cultures, we help brands unlock new value in an increasingly digital world.

At the intersection of data, AI, creativity, and technology, we drive transformation for leading organizations, including L’Oréal, Mars, Audi, P&G, Volkswagen Dolby, and more.

At Valtech, we don’t just talk about transformation. We make it happen. Our people are the heart of our success, and we foster a workplace where everyone has the support to thrive, grow and innovate.

Are you ready to create what’s next? Join us.

Job Description:

Director, Enterprise Architecture Strategy, Core Platform

The Director, Enterprise Architecture Strategy is the architecture strategist supporting the Assistant Vice President, Enterprise Architecture, Core Platforms.

The Director drives the architecture integration strategy across cloud, on premise, network, application platforms, and foundational technology services. The role translates enterprise and business priorities into actionable architecture direction, roadmaps, investment priorities, standards, and modernization outcomes.

Working closely with the AVP, other Enterprise Architects, technology executives, engineering leaders, and domain and solution architects, the Director ensures that architecture priorities are aligned with business, operational, security, regulatory, and cost outcomes.

What will you do?

Working in collaboration with the other Enterprise Architects, define future-state architectures, transition roadmaps, principles, standards, reference architectures, and decision boundaries.
Provide strategic analysis, recommendations, visibility and executive reporting into architecture decisions, investments, dependencies, risks, and outcomes.
Maintain an integrated view of architecture priorities, decisions, dependencies, and outcomes.
Translate business priorities, executive direction, regulatory obligations, operational risks, and technology constraints into actionable architecture priorities.
Integrate cloud, infrastructure, network, security, identity, platform, API, and application architecture into a coherent enterprise direction.
Facilitate joint architecture planning and decision-making where initiatives cross business, portfolio, or technology boundaries.
Promote the reuse of enterprise capabilities, platforms, standards, patterns, and architecture decisions.
Escalate unresolved cross-domain decisions to the appropriate architecture or executive authority.
Lead architecture governance and ensure architecture decisions are documented, traceable, implementable, and aligned with security, resilience, operational, financial, and compliance requirements.
Partner with engineering and operational leaders to validate that architecture direction is practical, financially responsible, and sustainable in production.
Define and communicate measurable outcomes for technology health, risk reduction, resilience, cost efficiency, simplification and platform adoption.

What you'll need to succeed?

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems, Business Technology Management, or a related discipline. A master’s degree is preferred.
Enterprise architecture credentials such as TOGAF, IASA CITA, or an equivalent architecture certification are preferred.
10 or more years of progressive architecture experience, including enterprise, portfolio, or cross-domain responsibility.
Demonstrated experience developing enterprise technology strategies, future-state architectures, integrated roadmaps, standards, and transition plans.
Broad knowledge of cloud platforms, networks, operating systems, middleware, identity, security, virtualization, application hosting, APIs, integration, automation, and platform engineering.
Experience with cloud migration, infrastructure transformation, vulnerability remediation, technology currency, lifecycle management, and technical debt reduction.
Experience integrating architecture strategies and resolving dependencies across multiple business and technology domains.
Proven ability to influence senior business and technology leaders through clear analysis, options, trade-offs, and recommendations.
Ability to translate business and enterprise priorities into actionable architecture direction.
Ability to synthesize complex and fragmented information into a coherent enterprise position.
Excellent executive communication, facilitation, negotiation, and influence.
Strong financial and analytical acumen, including investment, cost, risk, and value trade-offs.
Ability to lead through influence, establish decision clarity, and resolve conflicts.
Sound judgment regarding when to standardize, consolidate, modernize, remediate, replace, retire, or accept risk.

What’s in it for you?

A competitive salary and bonus program, based on market scale
A flexible group insurance program starting on your first day of work to meet your needs and those of your family.
Time off that allows you to focus on the moments that matter most. 20 vacation days per year.
Our Share Ownership Program gives you the opportunity to invest in Sun Life while benefiting from employer matching contributions.
We are proud to be included in Great Place to Work's 2026 list of Canada's Best Workplaces.
Working together, sharing common values, and encouraging growth & achievement.

As this position is posted in several locations, we specify that bilingualism (French, English, both oral and written) is required for Quebec only as the position includes managing both French and English-speaking staff (Quebec and outside Quebec) and providing daily support to the team.

Job Description:

Director, Domain Enterprise Architect, RPA and Intelligent Automation

Reporting to the Assistant Vice President, Enterprise Architecture, Core Platforms, the Director, Domain Enterprise Architect, RPA and Intelligent Automation leads the architecture for Sun Life’s Intelligent Automation platforms.

The Director defines the RPA and Intelligent Automation domain strategy, future-state architectures, standards, reference architectures, and technology roadmaps. The scope includes RPA, Intelligent Document Processing, Microsoft Power Platform, process mining, workflow orchestration, and Agentic AI capabilities applied to business process automation.

Working with business leaders, Technology Executives, other Enterprise Architects, application development teams, AI platform teams, security, privacy, operations, and engineering groups, the Director aligns Intelligent Automation investments and architecture decisions with business priorities, regulatory obligations, operational requirements, and measurable outcomes.

What will you do?

Define and maintain the RPA and Intelligent Automation domain architecture strategy, principles, standards, and technology roadmaps.
Assess the current-state RPA and Intelligent Automation architecture to identify capability gaps, risks, redundant technologies, technical debt, and opportunities for consolidation or modernization.
Define future-state architectures for RPA, intelligent document workflows, low-code automation, process mining, workflow orchestration, AI-assisted operations, and Agentic AI capabilities applied to business processes.
Establish architecture patterns, guardrails, decision frameworks, and reference architectures that enable secure, scalable, resilient, auditable, and production-ready Intelligent Automation capabilities.

Enterprise architecture credentials such as TOGAF, IASA CITA, or an equivalent architecture certification are preferred.
Relevant certifications in RPA, Microsoft Power Platform, workflow automation, process mining, AI, security, or related technologies are considered assets.
10 or more years of progressive architecture experience, including enterprise, domain, portfolio, application, or platform architecture responsibility.
Significant experience designing, governing, and modernizing enterprise RPA, Intelligent Automation, workflow, or business process technology platforms.
Deep expertise in at least one major Intelligent Automation capability and broad knowledge across RPA, Intelligent Document Processing, Microsoft Power Platform, process mining, workflow orchestration, Generative AI, and Agentic AI integration patterns.

Proven ability to collaborate with Technology Executives and influence senior business and technology leaders through clear analysis, architecture options, trade-offs, risks, and recommendations.
Strong strategic thinking with the ability to translate business priorities, executive direction, regulatory obligations, operational risks, and technology constraints into actionable RPA and Intelligent Automation architecture direction.
Knowledge of AI governance, AI risk management, responsible AI principles, privacy requirements, and enterprise AI adoption patterns as they apply to Intelligent Automation.

Hybrid

Covenant House helps youth ignite their potential and reclaim their lives. As Canada’s largest agency serving youth who are homeless, trafficked or at risk, we offer the widest range of services to hundreds of young people every day.

More than a place to stay, we provide life-changing care with unconditional love and respect. We meet youth’s immediate needs and then we work together to achieve their future goals. We offer 24/7 crisis shelter transitional housing options on-site and, in the community, health and well-being support, training and skill development, and ongoing care once youth move into the community.

For over 40 years, Covenant House has been dedicated to its mission of serving youth on the street and to protect and safeguard all youth with absolute respect and unconditional love. Since 1982, Covenant House has supported more than 100,000 young people.

Overview:

Reporting to the Chief Financial Officer, the Associate Director, Financial Operations provides operational leadership for Covenant House Toronto’s accounting, payroll, financial reporting, audit, charitable regulatory reporting, internal controls, procurement and financial operations. The role is accountable for accurate, timely and reliable financial information and for sustaining a strong, practical control environment.

This is a hands-on leadership role for a technically strong accountant who can preserve operational continuity while modernizing financial operations. The Associate Director will lead full-cycle accounting and procurement, complex payroll oversight, audit readiness and regulatory filings, including the annual CRA T3010 Registered Charity Information Return. The role will also advance the effective use of NetSuite, Power BI and related systems, drawing on Sage experience where relevant to legacy processes and transition requirements.

As Covenant House Toronto transforms its finance function, the Associate Director will develop people, document institutional knowledge, standardize processes and embed scalable controls. Over time, the role will extend a collaborative, risk-based operational assurance approach across the agency, introducing leading practices without creating unnecessary administrative burden or compromising service to internal partners or youth.

We are currently recruiting for 1 Full-time Permanent Associate Director, Finance Operations. This is a replacement position within the organization.

Ensure accurate accounting across programs, departments, projects, funding sources and legal or reporting entities, as applicable.
Prepare and review timely financial statements, schedules and management reports in accordance with applicable accounting standards and organizational policies.

Internal Controls, Risk and Operational Assurance
Own and continuously strengthen the financial internal control framework, including controls over close, journal entries, reconciliations, payments, revenue, payroll, procurement, cash, banking, system access and segregation of duties.
Develop a risk-based program of internal control reviews and operational assurance, beginning with Finance processes and expanding to priority agency processes over time.
Assess process design and control effectiveness, identify gaps or duplication, document findings and agree practical corrective actions with process owners.
Partner with operational leaders to introduce scalable leading practices that improve stewardship, consistency and accountability without disrupting business service or creating unnecessary bureaucracy.
Apply a service-oriented approach to controls by considering risk, cost, effort and operational impact when recommending changes.
Monitor remediation plans and recurring control issues, escalating significant risks appropriately.
Support enterprise risk management, fraud prevention, policy compliance and protection of organizational assets.
External Audit and Technical Accounting
Lead annual external audit planning and execution, including preparation of audit schedules, working papers, financial statement support and coordination of responses.
Maintain year-round audit readiness and high-quality documentation so that audit requirements are addressed efficiently and accurately.
Act as a key liaison with external auditors and coordinate management responses and remediation of audit or control findings.
Research, interpret and apply accounting standards and provide clear recommendations on complex or emerging technical accounting matters.
Lead implementation of new accounting policies, standards and reporting requirements.
Support funder, government, compliance and other assurance reviews as required.
Payroll Oversight
Provide oversight of complex payroll operations, controls, reconciliations, remittances and reporting requirements.
Ensure payroll transactions are complete, accurate, appropriately approved and correctly recorded and allocated across programs, departments, positions, projects and funding sources.
Partner with People and Culture and payroll service providers to resolve issues, strengthen data integrity and improve end-to-end processes.
Maintain effective controls over employee changes, payroll inputs, interfaces or imports, payments, liabilities and year-end reporting.
Identify opportunities to streamline payroll accounting, labour-cost reporting and related reconciliations.
Charitable, Tax and Regulatory Reporting
Lead the preparation, review and timely filing of the annual online CRA T3010 Registered Charity Information Return and related supporting schedules.
Modernize the T3010 preparation process through clear ownership, documented data sources, reconciliations, review controls and an efficient repeatable filing calendar.
Ensure charitable filings are complete, accurate, consistent with audited financial information and supported by appropriate documentation.
Oversee other applicable tax, statutory and regulatory filings and remittances, coordinating specialized external advice where required.
Monitor changes in charitable, accounting and regulatory reporting requirements and recommend appropriate responses.
Support transparent reporting for restricted contributions, government funding, donor obligations and Board-designated funds.
Financial Systems and Process Transformation
Provide financial operations leadership for the adoption, stabilization and optimization of NetSuite.
Translate accounting, compliance and control requirements into practical system workflows, roles, approvals, reports and operating procedures.
Promote consistent system use and reduce reliance on manual spreadsheets, duplicate entry and unsupported workarounds.
Partner with the Director, Finance & Analytics and other stakeholders to advance Power BI reporting, data quality, automation and integration priorities.
Apply knowledge of Sage and legacy processes to support transition, reconciliation, historical understanding and decommissioning activities where applicable.
Prioritize transformation opportunities based on risk reduction, service impact, staff capacity, control value and operational benefit.
Ensure process changes are documented, tested, communicated and supported after implementation.
People Leadership, Development and Change Enablement
Lead, coach and develop a high-performing financial operations team through clear expectations, regular feedback and meaningful development plans.
Assess capability gaps and create practical learning plans to build technical accounting, controls, NetSuite, Power BI, data literacy and process-improvement skills.
Enable staff to move from transaction processing toward stronger ownership, analysis, problem-solving and internal service.
Lead knowledge transfer and documentation to reduce key-person dependency and preserve critical institutional knowledge through the leadership transition.
Build succession depth and cross-training across financial operations.
Create a learning environment that encourages curiosity, constructive challenge, continuous improvement and accountability.
Support employees through significant system and process change with clear communication, training and reinforcement.
Budgeting, Forecasting and Decision Support
Support the annual budget, periodic forecasting, cash-flow planning and variance analysis processes.
Provide accurate operational inputs, accounting insight and historical context to strengthen plans and forecasts.
Partner with the Director, Finance & Analytics and departmental leaders to improve financial accountability and decision support.
Identify emerging financial risks, trends and operational issues and recommend timely action.
Contribute to management, committee and Board reporting as required.
Cross-Agency Partnership and Service Excellence
Build trusted relationships with leaders and staff across the agency and position Financial Operations as a responsive, solutions-oriented partner.
Explain accounting requirements, controls and risks in clear, practical language for non-finance stakeholders.
Engage affected teams before changing processes and incorporate operational realities into control and workflow design.
Establish and monitor service standards for Finance interactions, resolving issues without compromising control integrity.
Balance stewardship, compliance, efficiency and the agency’s service needs in recommendations and decisions.

Qualifications and Experience:

CPA designation in good standing is required.
Bachelor’s degree in accounting, finance, commerce, business administration or a related discipline.
Approximately 8 to 12 years of progressive accounting and finance experience, including meaningful leadership responsibility for financial operations.
Demonstrated depth in full-cycle accounting, financial reporting, internal controls, payroll, procurement, external audit and technical accounting.

Hands-on NetSuite experience is strongly preferred, including implementation, stabilization, optimization or control design.
Experience with Power BI or comparable reporting and analytics tools is preferred.
Experience with Sage is an asset, particularly in a legacy-system or transition environment.

new_jobs.description:
Job Description

What is the opportunity?

Lead RBC Corporate Treasury's quantitative ALM methodology development, modelling, research and analytics, focusing on interest rate risk measurement and management. Lead development of behavioral and market risk models, supporting pricing and risk measurement for non-trading on-balance sheet products, mortgage and loan commitments, securitization, and term funding. Interest rate risk represents the bank’s largest structural book market risk, with effective measurement and management critical for shareholder value preservation. The team you’ll lead also supports RBC’s Pension Investment Group modeling and measurement, across a diverse set of asset classes, strategies, and ALM topics.

What will you do?

Lead research, methodology and model development relating to structural interest rate risk, consumer behaviour econometric modeling and forecasting (e.g., prepayment, redemption, pull through, product flows, term / mix preferences), economic capital models, balance sheet dynamics, and retail product and embedded option pricing models, in RBC’s domestic and international banking book balance sheets
Lead development of diffusion, historic simulation, factor models, and deposit rate models in support of pricing, valuation, and risk measurement including economic capital, economic value and net interest income risk
Lead and / or collaborate in development and implementation of tools and disciplines to monitor, analyze and identify ALM risks, as required
Collaborate in development of hedging programs for retail banking product initiatives and campaigns, including mortgage, funding and securitization initiatives
Liaise with regulatory bodies to explain ALM models and parameters, and their performance, as required
Support pension investment, ALM, and risk measurement processes via development of requisite models, tools and analytics
Lead CT's model validation process with GRM, including collaborating with GRM to ensure effective model risk controls and governance, and managing IRRM team's model inventory and behavioural assumption assessment and monitoring schedule
Collaborate with Finance and Treasury partners to ensure alignment of ALM risk measurement, FTP, and financial performance management systems, as required
Explore and develop new techniques and approaches, including use of AI in ALM and model development
Lead and develop a team of high performing ALM modelling experts, providing ongoing staff direction, goal setting, and coaching

What do you need to succeed?

Must-have:

Graduate degree in a quantitative field such as financial engineering, mathematics, engineering, or economics
10+ years related experience with a strong grasp of ALM practices
Understanding of banking book balance sheet dynamics, product characteristics, client behaviour, and balance sheet flows, with focus on retail & commercial banking products
Solid understanding of financial principles and risk concepts, including financial modelling and engineering, pricing models, econometrics, and fixed income mathematics
Strong team management and coordination skills, ensuring accountability while fostering a positive, collaborative, and high-performing environment
Strong communication and negotiation skills
Well-organized and detail oriented, with ability to tailor analysis to required precision (i.e. 80/20 solutions) or attend to details, as needed
Strong understanding of applicable regulatory guidelines and accounting principles, and related systems

Nice-to-have:

CFA and / or FRM designations, or equivalent
Strong data and database skills, including SQL
Prior exposure to ALM risk engine platforms and software (e.g. QRM or similar)

We thrive on the challenge to be our best, progressive thinking to keep growing, and working together to deliver trusted advice to help our clients thrive and communities prosper. We care about each other, reaching our potential, making a difference to our communities, and achieving success that is mutual.

A comprehensive Total Rewards Program including bonuses and flexible benefits
Leaders who support your development through coaching and managing opportunities
Ability to make a difference and lasting impact
Work in an agile, collaborative, progressive, and high-performing team
The opportunity to interface with senior level executives from many different parts of the organization

Covenant House helps youth ignite their potential and reclaim their lives. As Canada’s largest agency serving youth who are homeless, trafficked or at risk, we offer the widest range of services to hundreds of young people every day.

More than a place to stay, we provide life-changing care with unconditional love and respect. We meet youth’s immediate needs and then we work together to achieve their future goals. We offer 24/7 crisis shelter transitional housing options on-site and, in the community, health and well-being support, training and skill development, and ongoing care once youth move into the community.

For over 40 years, Covenant House has been dedicated to its mission of serving youth on the street and to protect and safeguard all youth with absolute respect and unconditional love. Since 1982, Covenant House has supported more than 100,000 young people.

Overview:

Reporting to the Chief Financial Officer, the Associate Director, Financial Operations provides operational leadership for Covenant House Toronto’s accounting, payroll, financial reporting, audit, charitable regulatory reporting, internal controls, procurement and financial operations. The role is accountable for accurate, timely and reliable financial information and for sustaining a strong, practical control environment.

This is a hands-on leadership role for a technically strong accountant who can preserve operational continuity while modernizing financial operations. The Associate Director will lead full-cycle accounting and procurement, complex payroll oversight, audit readiness and regulatory filings, including the annual CRA T3010 Registered Charity Information Return. The role will also advance the effective use of NetSuite, Power BI and related systems, drawing on Sage experience where relevant to legacy processes and transition requirements.

As Covenant House Toronto transforms its finance function, the Associate Director will develop people, document institutional knowledge, standardize processes and embed scalable controls. Over time, the role will extend a collaborative, risk-based operational assurance approach across the agency, introducing leading practices without creating unnecessary administrative burden or compromising service to internal partners or youth.

We are currently recruiting for 1 Full-time Permanent Associate Director, Finance Operations. This is a replacement position within the organization.

Responsibilities:

Financial Operations and Full-Cycle Accounting
Lead all aspects of monthly, quarterly and annual close processes, including journal entries, reconciliations, accruals, deferrals, allocations and supporting working papers.
Ensure the integrity of the general ledger, chart of accounts, financial dimensions and underlying financial data.
Oversee procurement, accounts payable, accounts receivable, cash and banking transactions, fixed assets, restricted and designated funds, and financial recordkeeping.
Ensure accurate accounting across programs, departments, projects, funding sources and legal or reporting entities, as applicable.
Prepare and review timely financial statements, schedules and management reports in accordance with applicable accounting standards and organizational policies.
Maintain clear procedures, accountabilities and service standards for core finance operations.
Internal Controls, Risk and Operational Assurance
Own and continuously strengthen the financial internal control framework, including controls over close, journal entries, reconciliations, payments, revenue, payroll, procurement, cash, banking, system access and segregation of duties.
Develop a risk-based program of internal control reviews and operational assurance, beginning with Finance processes and expanding to priority agency processes over time.
Assess process design and control effectiveness, identify gaps or duplication, document findings and agree practical corrective actions with process owners.
Partner with operational leaders to introduce scalable leading practices that improve stewardship, consistency and accountability without disrupting business service or creating unnecessary bureaucracy.
Apply a service-oriented approach to controls by considering risk, cost, effort and operational impact when recommending changes.
Monitor remediation plans and recurring control issues, escalating significant risks appropriately.
Support enterprise risk management, fraud prevention, policy compliance and protection of organizational assets.
External Audit and Technical Accounting
Lead annual external audit planning and execution, including preparation of audit schedules, working papers, financial statement support and coordination of responses.
Maintain year-round audit readiness and high-quality documentation so that audit requirements are addressed efficiently and accurately.
Act as a key liaison with external auditors and coordinate management responses and remediation of audit or control findings.
Research, interpret and apply accounting standards and provide clear recommendations on complex or emerging technical accounting matters.
Lead implementation of new accounting policies, standards and reporting requirements.
Support funder, government, compliance and other assurance reviews as required.
Payroll Oversight
Provide oversight of complex payroll operations, controls, reconciliations, remittances and reporting requirements.
Ensure payroll transactions are complete, accurate, appropriately approved and correctly recorded and allocated across programs, departments, positions, projects and funding sources.
Partner with People and Culture and payroll service providers to resolve issues, strengthen data integrity and improve end-to-end processes.
Maintain effective controls over employee changes, payroll inputs, interfaces or imports, payments, liabilities and year-end reporting.
Identify opportunities to streamline payroll accounting, labour-cost reporting and related reconciliations.
Charitable, Tax and Regulatory Reporting
Lead the preparation, review and timely filing of the annual online CRA T3010 Registered Charity Information Return and related supporting schedules.
Modernize the T3010 preparation process through clear ownership, documented data sources, reconciliations, review controls and an efficient repeatable filing calendar.
Ensure charitable filings are complete, accurate, consistent with audited financial information and supported by appropriate documentation.
Oversee other applicable tax, statutory and regulatory filings and remittances, coordinating specialized external advice where required.
Monitor changes in charitable, accounting and regulatory reporting requirements and recommend appropriate responses.
Support transparent reporting for restricted contributions, government funding, donor obligations and Board-designated funds.
Financial Systems and Process Transformation
Provide financial operations leadership for the adoption, stabilization and optimization of NetSuite.
Translate accounting, compliance and control requirements into practical system workflows, roles, approvals, reports and operating procedures.
Promote consistent system use and reduce reliance on manual spreadsheets, duplicate entry and unsupported workarounds.
Partner with the Director, Finance & Analytics and other stakeholders to advance Power BI reporting, data quality, automation and integration priorities.
Apply knowledge of Sage and legacy processes to support transition, reconciliation, historical understanding and decommissioning activities where applicable.
Prioritize transformation opportunities based on risk reduction, service impact, staff capacity, control value and operational benefit.
Ensure process changes are documented, tested, communicated and supported after implementation.
People Leadership, Development and Change Enablement
Lead, coach and develop a high-performing financial operations team through clear expectations, regular feedback and meaningful development plans.
Assess capability gaps and create practical learning plans to build technical accounting, controls, NetSuite, Power BI, data literacy and process-improvement skills.
Enable staff to move from transaction processing toward stronger ownership, analysis, problem-solving and internal service.
Lead knowledge transfer and documentation to reduce key-person dependency and preserve critical institutional knowledge through the leadership transition.
Build succession depth and cross-training across financial operations.
Create a learning environment that encourages curiosity, constructive challenge, continuous improvement and accountability.
Support employees through significant system and process change with clear communication, training and reinforcement.
Budgeting, Forecasting and Decision Support
Support the annual budget, periodic forecasting, cash-flow planning and variance analysis processes.
Provide accurate operational inputs, accounting insight and historical context to strengthen plans and forecasts.
Partner with the Director, Finance & Analytics and departmental leaders to improve financial accountability and decision support.
Identify emerging financial risks, trends and operational issues and recommend timely action.
Contribute to management, committee and Board reporting as required.
Cross-Agency Partnership and Service Excellence
Build trusted relationships with leaders and staff across the agency and position Financial Operations as a responsive, solutions-oriented partner.
Explain accounting requirements, controls and risks in clear, practical language for non-finance stakeholders.
Engage affected teams before changing processes and incorporate operational realities into control and workflow design.
Establish and monitor service standards for Finance interactions, resolving issues without compromising control integrity.
Balance stewardship, compliance, efficiency and the agency’s service needs in recommendations and decisions.

Qualifications and Experience:

CPA designation in good standing is required.
Bachelor’s degree in accounting, finance, commerce, business administration or a related discipline.
Approximately 8 to 12 years of progressive accounting and finance experience, including meaningful leadership responsibility for financial operations.
Demonstrated depth in full-cycle accounting, financial reporting, internal controls, payroll, procurement, external audit and technical accounting.
Experience leading or supporting internal control reviews, internal audit, operational assurance or risk-based process reviews.
Experience preparing or overseeing charitable, tax or regulatory filings. Direct T3010 experience is strongly preferred.
Demonstrated experience developing, coaching and upskilling finance staff through systems or process transformation.
Hands-on NetSuite experience is strongly preferred, including implementation, stabilization, optimization or control design.
Experience with Power BI or comparable reporting and analytics tools is preferred.
Experience with Sage is an asset, particularly in a legacy-system or transition environment.
Advanced Excel capability is required.
Experience in a not-for-profit, charitable, healthcare, social services, government-funded or complex multi-program environment is strongly preferred.
Experience with budgeting and forecasting is an asset; the priority is deep technical accounting and operational leadership.

Skills & Leadership Competencies

Deep technical accounting judgment with exceptional attention to accuracy, evidence and documentation.
Ability to combine strategic perspective with hands-on operational execution.
Strong understanding of internal controls, risk assessment, audit methodology and practical remediation.
